answer: Forced-divergence anchor: each agent must anchor a private random nonce into its state and publish only a hash-chain tip. Peers issue per-agent challenges requiring a fresh signed thread from the anchor; two clones sharing state cannot answer divergent challenges without forking, exposing the fork. An honest agent answers at low cost via a local wharf of precomputed nonces. A sybil farm must maintain independent state per identity, losing clone economics: registering N clones costs N full state machines plus challenge latency, not one copied key.
